newsitem.title: UK: Sea Containers raps UK rail sell-off rule.
newsitem.headline: Sea Containers raps UK rail sell-off rule.

text.p: Sea Containers, one of three firms bidding for a British railway franchise, has criticised the British Government over its privatisation proposals which commit the sucessful bidder to a big investment in the route.

The Government is seeking guarantees from the successful bidder for InterCity West Coast (ICWC) network -- Britain's busiest intercity passenger line -- that it pledges, at the time of bid, large sums to upgrade the line.
Sea Containers, the Bermuda-based container leasing, transport and hotels group, is one of three bidding for the ICWC franchise along with Stagecoach Holdings and Virgin Group.

James Sherwood, Sea Containers president, said since unproven technology would be involved in the project, it would mean substantial capital outlay, posing a financial risk for the prospective franchisee.
Thursday is the deadline for submitting bids to Sir George Young, Secretary of State for Transport and rail watchdog OPRAF to take over ICWC.
Sea Containers already owns the InterCity East Coast line through its subsidiary Great North Eastern Railway (GNER).
Sherwood said he had had an "open and frank discussion" with Young over what he described as a problem with his company's West Coast bid.
"The Government is seeking not only to privatize InterCity West Coast but to obtain a guaranteed upgrade of the network in the process," Sherwood said.

"I'm not certain the two can be completely linked at this stage," he added. "We must be certain that new technology works on the British Rail system and the requirements of financial institutions are fully met."

Sherwood considered it likely the Government would have to sit down with each prospective franchisee and talk through various business plan issues. Cost of upgrading track and signalling alone would cost 300 million stg.
He added that OPRAF was committed to handing out the West Coast franchise by April 1. Sources speculate that the name of the successful bidder could be known as soon as February 7.
